cards.title: Practice, honestly
cards.text: 457 laps run and nothing at stake. What it does tell you is who looks comfortable and who is fighting the car.

cards.title: Russell: 1:43.347
cards.text: In a Mercedes. Take practice times with salt: fuel loads are secret and nobody shows their hand.

cards.title: Bottas racked up 25 laps
cards.text: Track time is the currency of a Friday. Whoever runs most learns most, and burns the most rubber doing it.

cards.title: Hamilton looked strongest over a stint
cards.text: Average clean lap across the session. This is the number teams actually care about on a Friday, not the headline time.

cards.title: What they ran, and on what
cards.text: Compound choice on a Friday is a rehearsal for Sunday's plan.

cards.title: Hadjar topped the trap at 339 km/h
cards.text: Early wing choices show up here before anybody admits to them.

cards.title: 35 flag calls, and the session stopped once
cards.text: A red flag sends everybody back to the pits and the clock keeps running. Whatever run you were on is gone, and so is the time to repeat it.

cards.title: Track between 41°C and 49°C
cards.text: Friday conditions rarely match Sunday, which is why the times you see here mislead so often.
